Subject: Pricing qualification — token benchmarking

Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can benchmark pricing for your use case.

Recap from our call:
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat + extractive QA for knowledge base (~95% read, 5% write).
- Models: you expect to evaluate both Llama-family / Mistral open models and endpoint comparisons vs OpenAI/Anthropic for fall back.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 1–2k token responses.
- Security: data residency in us-east, SOC2 required (we covered Redwood Private options).

As discussed, to produce a tailored price comparison we need the following from you:
1) Expected token volumes (monthly): read (prompt+response) and write separately if possible.
2) Budget range for inference (monthly committed / preferred target $/1M tokens).
3) Any peak-day or burst characteristics (x% of traffic on peak days).

If easier, attach a quick spreadsheet with the volumes — I can slot numbers into our unit economics model and return a short benchmark vs OpenAI/Anthropic and hosted open-model providers.

Next steps I propose:
- You send token volume sheet (if available) — we’ll return a 1‑page benchmarking summary and recommended target price bands (Redwood recommended target $/1M, competitor comparators) within 48 hours.
- If the numbers look good, we can propose a pilot with a reserved capacity discount to hit your SLAs.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks for the recap. See attached high-level estimates. A few clarifications inline:
- Monthly traffic: 120M user interactions (most are short prompts).
- Average tokens per interaction: prompt 120 tokens / response 220 tokens => ~340 tokens per interaction.
- Monthly tokens: ~40.8B tokens total (we split as: prompt ~14.4B, response ~26.4B).
- Peak: 2x baseline during product launches (10% of monthly concentrated into 3–4 days).

Budget: leadership gave a target range of $10k–$25k/month for inference initially while we validate LLM features (we can expand later). They asked us to find target $/1M that would achieve the monthly cost objective.

Quick ask: can you produce a short comparison showing what the unit cost would need to be (target $/1M) across these volumes to fit the $10k–$25k budget band, and how that compares to OpenAI/Anthropic and hosted open-model providers?

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing qualification — token benchmarking / target $/1M

Alex —

Thanks for the spreadsheet — helpful. Below is a 1‑page summary with the target $/1M math and competitor benchmarks. I attached a short PDF snapshot of our pricing model and assumptions.

Summary (assumptions: 40.8B monthly tokens total):
- To hit $10k/month => target effective price = $0.000245 per 1,000 tokens => $0.245 per 1M tokens (note: this is aggressively low and would require heavy caching, large discounts via committed reserved capacity, and significant quantization/opt. It may not be feasible for closed-source hosted endpoints).
- To hit $25k/month => target effective price = $0.000613 per 1,000 tokens => $0.613 per 1M tokens.

Practically, we usually express cost in $/1M tokens (not per 1K). Converting your bands:
- Target band (derived from budget): ~$0.25 — $0.61 per 1M tokens (net effective).

Competitor benchmarks (indicative market rates, public and observed host deals for chat-type workloads):
- OpenAI (GPT-family managed endpoints): ~ $10 — $40 per 1M tokens depending on model (higher for GPT-4 style), typical PLG customers see $10–$20/1M for lighter models.
- Anthropic (Claude endpoints): ~ $8 — $30 per 1M tokens depending on model and contract.
- Hosted open-model providers (managed Mistral/Llama): ~ $2 — $12 per 1M tokens (varies a lot based on instance type, quantization, caching).
- Self-hosted (on-prem with strong optimization): can be sub-$1 per 1M tokens at very large scale but requires ops investment and hardware amortization.

Redwood positioning and recommended target:
- For your volume profile (40.8B tokens/month) and latency SLO, a realistic Redwood target after committed reserved capacity + optimizations would be in the range: $0.5 — $6 per 1M tokens depending on the model family and fallback policy.
- Practical recommendation: we should run a 30‑day pilot on a mixed model strategy: primary on a highly cost‑optimized open-model variant (quantized + prefix caching) and fallback to a managed endpoint only for difficult queries. This typically brings net cost down towards the lower end of the chart.

Next steps:
1) We’ll produce a short cost model (spreadsheet) that takes your attached estimates and maps to three scenarios: conservative (OpenAI/Anthropic-first), mixed (open-model primary + fallbacks), and optimized‑at‑scale (open-model with reserved capacity). Expect that by EOD tomorrow. (see related HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ACME-3452)
2) If the mixed/optimized scenarios align with your $10k–$25k band, we’ll propose a pilot + reserved capacity pricing and a short runbook for performance validation.
3) Marissa will follow up on contractual and SOC2 checklist items if you want to proceed.

Attachment: redwood_pricing_snapshot.pdf (PDF) — includes our assumptions, per‑model cost bands, and an example reserved capacity offer.

Let me know if you want a quick 20-minute sync to walk through the spreadsheet results.

Thanks,
